messages.subject: simple example of dynamic drop down list--thanks to earlier posts and tutorial
parts:
This is related to the question posed by Cindy Hart but not a solution to her questions.  I built a toy example that illustrates a dynamically populated drop down list and post it here to help other new users learn more about dynamic tools in shiny.  I am interested in getting dynamic controls specific to tabs, will follow up the other string for that.

The problem is motivated by an analysis of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services payment data set, which consists of ~160,000 payment records from 2011, organized by diagnostic related group (DRG); state; and hospital within state.  

I want to allow the user to select a DRG and a state in drop down lists in the UI (these lists do not need to be defined dynamically).  Then given this information, populate a third drop down list of hospitals for the specific state and DRG for further analysis.  I create the list of hospital names for each state once in the global code and just select the correct hospital list given the state name.    I think this may be faster than creating the list on the fly but I did not tests.

The example creates summaries of data, the actual application has a set of scatter plot--the hard part for me was getting the dynamic drop down list to work.
